>> Hey, thanks for a great question, Joe.
And you're absolutely right. If you look
at all the tithes that are prescribed
across the Hebrew Bible, there are
multiple of them and they would add up
to 20% or more, although some of them
are less frequent than others. And the
reason for this is because they belong
to different literary layers. And when
those literary layers were initially
proliferated, they either superseded any
authoritative
literary layer that came before or this
happened independent of the other
literary layers because you have a
tithe. The earliest one that we
reconstruct is one that is more about
sharing with the underprivileged in your
community and with the local priesthood
and priests. And then when you get
centralized worship in Jerusalem, you
have a tithe that is supposed to come
into the temple in Jerusalem. And then
later on with the priestly layer, you
have a tithe that is specifically for
the Levitical priesthood. And so these
are intended to serve uh different
interests and either supersede or
function independently of other tithes.
And it's not until all the texts are
gathered together and are considered a
single authoritative corpus that you
suddenly have to deal with compounded
tithing requirements. And so you have
some Jewish texts that uh will say,
well, yeah, you're supposed to do this
one, then the other one, then the other
one. And yeah, that's a big chunk of
your income. But the majority of folks
said, no, you don't have to do all of
them all at the same time. So it depends
on what tradition you're looking at. But
yeah, the tithe is not something that is
consistent throughout the Hebrew Bible.
Like all of the Bible, it is not
univocal. It is multivocal. These are
different folks writing to different
audiences for different reasons in
different time periods. And so it is an
artifact of our bringing all these texts
together and saying they function as one
single unified and consistent corpus
that results in compounding the tithes.
